QF.id: AIFM Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_11

question.text: Capital Market Theory (CMT) extends Modern Portfolio Theory by adding a risk-free asset. Which of the following is NOT an assumption of CMT as set out in Chapter 5 of the XIX-C workbook?

answer.text: Investors have heterogeneous investment horizons and each investor solves a multi-period utility maximisation problem.
All investors can lend and borrow any amount at the risk-free rate of return.
All investors have homogeneous expectations about asset returns.
There are no taxes or transaction costs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 5.2 assumes a single, identical one-period horizon for all investors (not multi-period, not heterogeneous). The other three are explicit CMT assumptions: risk-free lend/borrow, homogeneous expectations, no taxes/transaction costs. The Trap: Option B ('borrow ANY amount') sounds demanding but is indeed a CMT assumption. Option C (homogeneous expectations) is the unique-to-CMT assumption on top of MPT. Option D is a frictionless-market assumption.
